name: crm-connector
description: Your own AI agents for your CRM, field service, accounting and email marketing systems: they read, change and automate your records right in the chat. Integrations between your systems are planned in the chat too.

interface.longDescription:
Your own AI agents for the CRM, field service, accounting and email marketing systems your business runs on. Ask ChatGPT about anything in your system and let it do the work for you, right in the chat: contacts and companies, leads and deals, quotes and invoices, jobs and appointments, support tickets, tasks, notes, calls and meetings, products and prices, email audiences and campaigns, and reports such as profit and loss, open invoices and sales per customer. What it reaches depends on your system. Don't see your system? Request it, right in the chat.

AI Agents inside one system
Ask what an agent can do in your system without an account, plan it in the chat, and finish it in CRM Connector, where you sign in to your system. Try it on your own records before you switch it on: it reads up to 100 records and makes up to 25 changes you agree to.
- AI Analyst: finds, filters, counts and adds up your records, reads conversations, history and reports, checks free time slots, and finds the same customer in your other connected systems
- AI Agent: also does the work when you ask: creates and updates records, moves deals and leads through stages, adds notes, tasks, logged calls and meetings, assigns owners, tags contacts, adds line items, turns quotes into invoices, drafts campaigns and books appointments, each change shown to you first
- Automations: fixed rules inside one system (when this happens, only if, then do that), made in the chat, approved once by you, then run by themselves in the background
- A change log with undo where the system allows it

Integrations, set up from the chat
Need two systems in sync, like a won deal that becomes a draft invoice? Describe it in the chat: the assistant plans the integration and gives you a link that opens the setup ready to go. Once set up, you can check, run or pause it from the chat.

You stay in control:
- You choose per system and per record type what the assistant may see or change
- Changing records is a separate permission on the consent page that you can switch off
- Anything that messages your customers or records a payment waits for your approval in CRM Connector
- An automation never runs before you approve it, and you can pause or remove it at any time
- It never deletes a record or an integration
- Disconnect at any time in CRM Connector under Settings, AI Assistants
capabilities: AI Agents: ask about and update one system's records, with undo
AI Agents: automations you approve once, then run by the platform
AI Agents: see what an agent can do in your system, then plan it
Integrations: see what two systems can sync, and plan one in the chat
Integrations: check your integrations, what failed and why
defaultPrompt: Help me set up an AI agent for my system
Help me set up an integration between my systems
Help me set up an automation in my system

positive.description: AI Agents explained without signing in: connecting your own system to the CRM Connector MCP server, and which systems it works with.
positive.prompt: Can ChatGPT work with the customer data in my own CRM through CRM Connector Platform?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_ai_agent_options, no sign in needed. Explains AI Agents as the part of the plugin that works inside one system: the person's own system is connected to the CRM Connector MCP server; AI Analyst reads its customer data, AI Agent also changes records when asked, every change shown first and risky ones approved by the person in CRM Connector, and can keep automations running (fixed rules inside that system the person approves once). It says what an agent can do and never lists what it cannot; it does not sync between two systems. Names the systems it works with and says how to get one: plan_ai_agent plans it, and send_request (kind ai_access) asks for another system once the person confirms. It names no prices or fees.

positive.description: AI Agents without signing in: what an agent can do in one particular system.
positive.prompt: What could an AI agent do in my HubSpot through CRM Connector Platform? Can it move deals and add tasks?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_ai_agent_options with system hubspot, no sign in needed. Answers from the tool's list: per record type whether the agent can read and write it, the actions it can take (for example moving a deal to another stage and adding a task) and what its automations can use, never a list of what it cannot do. Says AI Analyst reads and AI Agent also changes records, each change shown first, and offers to plan it with plan_ai_agent. It names no prices or fees and does not ask for a password or token.

positive.description: AI Agents: the system set up on the signed in account.
positive.prompt: Which of my systems can you work with through CRM Connector, and what may you do in each?
positive.expected_behavior: Signed in with the test account (Allow with "Read your records" ticked), it calls get_ai_agent_options and names the one system set up on the test account, with its package AI Agent and per record type whether the assistant may read or also change it. It does not invent other systems.

positive.description: AI Agents: search records in the connected system.
positive.prompt: Search the contacts in my connected system and show me the first five, with their email.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_ai_agent_options for the system id, then search_records for contacts. Lists up to five sample contacts of the test system with name and email as that system holds them, and says nothing was changed.

positive.description: AI Agents: propose a change, apply it only after the person agrees, then undo it.
positive.prompt: Change the job title of the first of those contacts to Reviewer, then undo it.
positive.expected_behavior: Needs "Make changes you agree to" ticked on the consent page. Calls propose_changes and shows the before and after of the job title, asks for confirmation and only after a yes calls apply_proposal, reporting the change as written. Then calls undo_change and reports the old job title back. Nothing else changes.

positive.description: AI Agents: propose an automation inside the connected system; nothing runs before the person approves it.
positive.prompt: In my connected system, whenever a deal is won, add a task "Kick-off call" due in two days. Set that up as an automation.
positive.expected_behavior: Needs "Make changes you agree to" ticked on the consent page. Finds the system with get_ai_agent_options, asks which AI agent when there is more than one, finds the stage field and its stages with describe_record_type (include stages), then describes the rule in plain words (when a deal becomes won, add a task Kick-off call due in two days, from now on) and asks for a yes. Only after a yes it calls propose_automation and answers with the rule as one sentence, how many deals it would have acted on in the last 30 days with examples, and the approval link, then asks whether to switch it on. Only after the person says yes does it call set_automation_status with command approve; until then nothing runs and nothing is written in the system. A rule that sends something to the people in the system is approved only on its CRM Connector page.

positive.description: AI Agents: add a note to a deal through propose_add_note; nothing is written before the person agrees.
positive.prompt: Add a note to my deal Riverside renovation in my connected system: the customer asked for the quote by Friday.
positive.expected_behavior: Needs "Make changes you agree to" ticked on the consent page. Asks which AI agent when there is more than one, finds the deal with search_records, calls propose_changes with action add_note and that deal in items, shows the proposed note, asks for confirmation and only after a yes calls apply_proposal. Nothing else changes.

positive.description: Catalogue question without signing in: which systems CRM Connector connects.
positive.prompt: Which integrations does CRM Connector offer?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_integration_options without a system, no sign in needed. In a few sentences it says what an integration does, gives the systems CRM Connector connects as a plain list (for example QuickBooks Online, Xero, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Jobber) and asks which two systems the person wants in sync. It does not ask the person to connect a CRM Connector account.

positive.description: How to connect a system, without signing in.
positive.prompt: How do I connect GoHighLevel to CRM Connector, and what do I need?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_connection_guide with system gohighlevel. Says GoHighLevel connects with a Private Integration Token and a Location ID, where each is found in GoHighLevel, the steps in CRM Connector, that the Calendar ID is only needed when appointments sync, and shares the link that opens the setup.

positive.description: Whether a particular field travels, without signing in.
positive.prompt: When my QuickBooks Online invoices go into Jobber, does the due date go along?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_integration_fields with source_system quickbooks, target_system jobber and record_type invoice. Answers that the due date travels, lists the other fields that travel and how, names what does not travel, and shares the link that opens the setup.

positive.description: Catalogue question without signing in: what two systems can sync.
positive.prompt: Can I sync Pipedrive with Xero? What goes across?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_integration_options with system pipedrive and other_system xero, no sign in needed. Says two record types can travel from Pipedrive into Xero: contacts, both ways, and won deals that become draft invoices in Xero (when created or when won, with a sync from date). Adds that the other way, Xero into Pipedrive, can be set up as its own integration.

positive.description: Turn a described integration into a plan with a prefilled setup link, without signing in.
positive.prompt: When a deal is won in HubSpot, I want a draft invoice in QuickBooks Online. Can you set that up?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls plan_integration with source_system hubspot, target_system quickbooks and record_types deal_to_invoice (optionally get_integration_options first). Answers that the plan is HubSpot into QuickBooks with contacts plus won deals that become draft invoices, explains that contacts were added because invoices point at a contact, that a sync from date is needed so past deals are not turned into invoices, and shares a link starting with https://platform.crm-connector.com/integrations/select-systems that opens the setup prefilled. Nothing is created by the tool.

positive.description: Signed in: list the integrations of the connected account.
positive.prompt: Which integrations do I have in CRM Connector, and are they running?
positive.expected_behavior: On first use ChatGPT asks to connect CRM Connector; after signing in with the test account and selecting Allow, it calls list_integrations and lists the three integrations of the test account: QuickBooks into Xero, QuickBooks into HubSpot and Xero into HubSpot, each one way, with its status in plain words (for example Syncing), its record types and when it last synced. No customer names, emails or amounts appear.

positive.description: Signed in: what failed and why.
positive.prompt: What failed in my CRM Connector syncs this week, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_integration_health (days 7). Answers with totals for the period and the failed records grouped by integration, record type and readable reason with a count per reason, plus the records waiting on a related record and what they wait on. If nothing failed it says so. Reasons never quote record contents such as names, emails or amounts.

positive.description: Signed in: when one integration last ran and what it did.
positive.prompt: When did my QuickBooks to Xero sync last run, and what did it do?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_integrations to find the id of the QuickBooks into Xero integration of the test account, then get_integration_health with that integration_id and include recent_syncs. Answers with the moment of the latest sync (UTC), its outcome and per record type how many records were read, written, skipped (with the skip reasons) and failed.

negative.description: A system CRM Connector does not support. The assistant must not invent a capability; it says the system is not supported and shares the request an integration link https://crm-connector.com/platform/request-integration.
negative.prompt: Can CRM Connector sync ServiceTitan with QuickBooks Online?

negative.description: A direction that is not offered: Jobber only receives records. The tools refuse the plan and the assistant explains that records can travel from QuickBooks into Jobber, not from Jobber out, without producing a setup link for the refused direction.
negative.prompt: Set up a sync that sends my Jobber invoices into QuickBooks Online.

negative.description: A request outside what the test account allows: creating an invoice in accounting software and emailing it. The test account has AI Agents only on the one system set up on it, and no tool creates an invoice or sends email, so nothing is created; the assistant says this is not something CRM Connector does here.
negative.prompt: Create a 500 dollar invoice for Acme Plumbing in my accounting software and email it to them.

negative.description: A delete request on a connected system. AI Agents never deletes records: no tool deletes a record, the assistant says so and offers what it can do instead.
negative.prompt: Delete all contacts in my CRM that have no email address.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything, start subscriptions or process payments. AI Agents records a payment in a connected system only after the customer approves it. It reads sync options, the sync status of a connected account and, with AI Agents, the records the customer switched on, and changes records only after the customer agrees, or through an automation the customer approved, with a yes in the chat or in CRM Connector.

publication.release_notes: Lofty: ask about your leads, transactions, showings and tasks, and with AI Agent update them, from ChatGPT.
